slides.title: Operations
slides.subtitle: Approve exactly what the company proposed, performed at most once, and recover a lost answer
slides.notes: An operation is an action a company performs only once the user approves its exact terms: a payment, an exchange, a cancellation. This example gets Ada's approval of Northwind Bank's payments with the Operations extension, version 2.

slides.title: Why operations
slides.statement: The approval is **exact** and **durable**: a chat message never approves anything.
slides.notes: Money moves only on an explicit approval of one revision of the terms. The user approves in the host's own interface, every time, and the company performs an approved action at most once, even when answers get lost.

slides.title: Who takes part
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR M["Model"] subgraph HOST["Ada's side, trusted"] direction TB U["Ada"] -- "approves" --> H["Atlas host
OperationsClient"] end subgraph CO["Northwind Bank"] direction TB B["Conversation or API
proposes, then performs"] end CO -- "operation: revision, summary, terms" --> HOST HOST -- "the same request, with the approval" --> CO HOST -. "summaries only" .-> M
slides.caption: Only Ada approves; the model can explain an operation but never approve it.
slides.notes: Start on the right: Northwind Bank proposes a payment, as an operation with a revision and its terms. On the left, inside Ada's trusted side, the Atlas host shows it to Ada, and she approves in the host's own interface. The host then makes the same request again, with her approval of that exact revision. Off to the side, the model receives summaries only, never the power to approve.

slides.title: Approval, and changed terms

items.title: Proposal
items.detail: An operation: EUR 1250.00 to Acme GmbH

items.title: New revision
items.detail: EUR 1262.50, a fee added: nothing done

slides.notes: Operations apply only when the bank and the agent both list the extension. Ada sees the summary and terms and approves that revision. The bank has since added a fee, so it performs nothing and returns a new revision of the same operation.

slides.title: Approve again, and recover

items.title: Answer lost
items.detail: The bank performed it; the reply never came

items.title: Send again
items.detail: The same approval: the original response

slides.notes: The host shows Ada which terms changed and she approves the new revision. The bank performs the payment but the answer is lost. The SDK sends the same request with the same approval, and the bank answers with its original response: the payment happens once.

slides.title: What an approval can meet
slides.diagram:
flowchart LR A["The request,
with an approval"] --> Q{"Revision accepted?"} Q -- "yes" --> P["Performed once,
the usual response"] Q -- "new terms, expired,
another request" --> N["Nothing done,
a new revision"] N --> ASK["Ask the user again"] P -- "sent again" --> R["The original response"] A -- "while it runs" --> W["503 with Retry-After"]
slides.caption: An operation has no state of its own: the answer to the approved request is the result.
slides.notes: An operation has no state, no URL and no result: the answer to the approved request is the result. Follow a request with an approval. If the company accepts the revision, it performs the action once and answers as usual, and a repeat gets that original response. If the revision is one it can't accept, because the terms changed, it expired, or it was for another request, the company performs nothing and returns a new revision, and the user is asked again. While the action is being performed, a repeat gets 503 with Retry-After. When no answer comes in the end the outcome is unknown, and the host finds out before it asks again.

slides.title: What stays where

right.heading: What the model sees
items: What the bank says it came to, as written

slides.notes: The model can explain what happened, but it cannot approve. Tokens and proofs stay in the host, and the decision stays with the user in the host's own interface.

slides.title: Run it yourself
slides.cta: The Pydantic AI and Agent Runtimes examples get Ada's approval of Northwind Bank's payments end to end
slides.notes: Run the Pydantic AI example with PAP_EXAMPLE_MODEL set to the model you want. TypeScript offers the same OperationsClient, with askUser and send, and the host's surface contributed at ApprovalSurfaces.
